title: Ending a marathon without owing pleasure

captions.physics: Rejecting a shared script that fails
captions.energy: Trying to hold a promised intensity

meaning: Shared leisure can change more freely when an unworkable form’s ending leaves you unbound by restoring earlier enjoyment through repetition at any cost.
text: A familiar script can survive through the promise of a feeling increasingly hard to obtain. The Tower in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes rejecting a programme with a mistaken foundation. The Devil in energy holds earlier enjoyment as the reward for continuing. Death in emotions allows that form’s ending to be experienced. This ends no possibility of pleasure together. Both may need to acknowledge a changed way of spending time without requiring the next meeting immediately to restore all its former richness.

For example, night-long film marathons have become an obligation to finish a series. Conversation disappears and amusing scenes pass unnoticed, yet another film seems likely to restore the excitement. **A script can end while earlier evenings keep their value.** You can turn the screen off and name today’s wish calmly. A short conversation can be enough even while sadness remains and neither has a ready new grand interest.

The difficulty is seeking the old feeling through a compulsory final repetition. You start another film to test whether interest really ended and struggle to hear a wish to stop. Pleasant history binds. Leaving the false condition helps when one particular form can finish. Memory can stay warm without continuation, while another scale needs no proof that the past was wrong or new closeness must become stronger.
